Setup your Better Thermostat to integrate with Home Assistant

**Detailed information:** {docs_url}

data.name: Name
data.min_cooler_resend_interval: Minimum seconds between repeated cooler commands (0 = disabled)
data.off_temperature: The outdoor temperature when the thermostat should turn off
data.tolerance: Tolerance, to prevent the thermostat from turning on and off too often
data.window_off_delay: Delay before the thermostat should turn off when the window is opened
data.window_off_delay_after: Delay before the thermostat should turn on when the window is closed
data.door_off_delay: Delay before the thermostat should turn off when the door is opened
data.door_off_delay_after: Delay before the thermostat should turn on when the door is closed
data.weather: Weather entity to get the outdoor temperature
data.boost_asymmetric_threshold: Use a different threshold for cooling

data_description.presets: Select the presets you want to be available for this thermostat.
data_description.underfloor_heating_enabled: Turn this on if any of your heaters are underfloor heating (UFH) loops. This unlocks a per-heater 'Heating type' option and Warm Floor mode, which keeps a low background heat level in the floor instead of letting it fully cool between heat calls.
data_description.show_all_calibration_modes: By default, a heater flagged 'Underfloor' only offers the calibration modes that work correctly for it (MPC Predictive, (AI) MPC v2, TPI Controller, PID Controller). Turn this on to see all 8 modes instead - useful if your underfloor loop is driven by a valve-capable actuator.
data_description.cooler: Optional. A device used for cooling (in heat+cool setups) and/or, once Boost is enabled below, as the device that quickly recovers room temperature after a window reopens - many fan-coils, heat pumps, and AC units already do both jobs, so one entity can serve both roles.
data_description.boost_heater_enabled: Turn this on to also use the Cooling / Boost device above for fast temperature recovery after a window reopens. If the room drifted colder than the threshold below while the window was open, closing it boosts the device to heat; if it drifted warmer (e.g. a hot day with cooling suppressed), closing it boosts the device to cool. Either way it targets your normal target temperature; once it ends, the device is restored to exactly what it was doing before the boost took over. Requires a Cooling / Boost device to be configured above.
data_description.boost_threshold: If the room temperature drifts (in either direction) by more than this while a window is open, closing the window arms the boost.
data_description.boost_fan_mode: Optionally set the device's fan speed (e.g. to maximum) while boosting; restored automatically once the boost ends. Leave as 'Don't change fan mode' to skip this.
data_description.boost_lag_minutes: How many minutes of residual heating/cooling the device keeps delivering into the room after being told to stop, used to avoid overshooting the target.
data_description.boost_max_runtime: Maximum time the boost is allowed to run before forcing it off regardless of temperature.
data_description.boost_asymmetric_threshold: Turn this on to set a separate drift threshold for arming a cool boost (e.g. a hot summer day) than for arming a heat boost. Leave off to use the same threshold for both directions.
data_description.boost_threshold_cool: If the room temperature rose by more than this while a window was open, closing it arms a cool boost. Only used when the toggle above is on.
data_description.boost_cooldown_minutes: Minimum time after a boost ends before another one can re-arm, so a room that keeps drifting past the threshold (e.g. repeated window in/out) doesn't short-cycle the shared device.

data.heat_auto_swapped: If 'auto' means 'heat' for your TRV and you want to swap it
data.child_lock: Ignore all inputs on the TRV like a child lock
data.homematicip: If you use HomematicIP, you should enable this to slow down the requests to prevent the duty cycle
data.valve_maintenance: If your thermostat has no own maintenance mode, you can use this one
data.no_off_system_mode: If your TRV doesn't support the 'off' mode, enable this to use target temperature 5°C instead

data_description.protect_overheating: Some TRVs don't close the valve completely when the temperature is reached. Or the radiator has a lot of rest heat. This can cause overheating. This option can prevent this.
data_description.calibration_mode:
How the calibration is calculated
***Normal***: Uses your external temperature sensor to correct the TRV's internal sensor. Simple and reliable for most setups.
***Aggressive***: Similar to Normal, but pushes the TRV harder to reach temperature faster. Good if your room heats slowly.
***AI Time Based***: Learns your room's heating patterns over time and adjusts automatically. Balances comfort and efficiency.
***MPC Predictive***: Advanced algorithm that predicts temperature changes and optimizes valve position. Best for stable, efficient heating with minimal overshooting. Learns your room's thermal behavior.
***PID Controller***: Classic control method that responds to temperature errors. Good for systems with varying heating power or external disturbances.
***TPI Controller***: Calculates heating duty cycles based on temperature difference. Simple and effective for consistent heating patterns.
data_description.calibration:
How the calibration is applied on the TRV
***Target Temperature Based***: Apply the calibration to the target temperature.
***Offset Based***: Apply the calibration to the temperature offset.
data_description.heating_type: Under: enables Warm Floor mode for this heater. Radiator/Fan-coil-Convector/AC-HVAC: normal TRV behavior for now - these labels exist so a mixed underfloor+secondary-device setup can identify each heater correctly.
data_description.warm_floor_level:
How hard Warm Floor works to keep this heater from fully idling. Controls both fields below together - pick 'Custom' to set them directly instead.
***1 · Eco***: Gentle, minimal extra energy use.
***2 · Balanced***: The default - a reasonable backoff allowance, no sustain push.
***3 · Keep it Hot***: Tightest backoff plus a small sustain push, for floors that must never feel cold.
data_description.warm_floor_max_backoff: How far below target temperature Warm Floor is allowed to let this heater's setpoint drift during what would otherwise be an idle cycle. The actual backoff used is automatically scaled down from this maximum based on measured heat loss, heating power, and solar gain, so the floor is only ever backed off as far as the room can safely afford.
data_description.warm_floor_sustain_push: For calibration modes that pin the setpoint at exactly target once idle (so the backoff above has nothing to raise), push the setpoint sent to the heater this much above target instead - only while the room has already reached target and stayed there. Never changes the target temperature you see on the card. 0 (default) disables this.

confirm.title: The related entity {entity} is missing
confirm.description:
The reason for this is that the entity ({entity}) is not available in your Home Assistant.

You can fix this by checking if the battery of the device is full or reconnecting it to HA. Make sure that the entity is back in HA before you continue.

degraded_mode.title: BT: {name} - sensor error: {sensors} running in degraded mode
degraded_mode.description:
Better Thermostat is running in degraded mode because some sensors are unavailable: {sensors}

The thermostat will continue to operate with reduced functionality. For example:
- If the room temperature sensor is unavailable, the TRV's internal sensor will be used instead.
- If a window or door sensor is unavailable, its last known state stays in effect: a contact that was closed keeps heating enabled, a contact that was open keeps heating suppressed until the sensor reports closed again. Only at startup is an unavailable contact sensor treated as closed.
- If outdoor/weather sensors are unavailable, heating will always be enabled.

Check if the affected devices have battery issues or connectivity problems.

invalid_window_state.title: BT: {name} - invalid window sensor state
invalid_window_state.description:
The window sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an unrecognized state: {state}.

Expected states are: 'on', 'off', 'true', 'false', 'open', 'closed'.

Please check your window sensor configuration.

invalid_door_state.title: BT: {name} - invalid door sensor state
invalid_door_state.description:
The door sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an unrecognized state: {state}.

Expected states are: 'on', 'off', 'true', 'false', 'open', 'closed'.

Please check your door sensor configuration.

invalid_external_temperature.title: BT: {name} - invalid external temperature
invalid_external_temperature.description:
The external temperature sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an implausible value: {value}.

The reading was outside the plausible range and has been ignored. Please check your temperature sensor configuration.

run_valve_maintenance.name: Run valve maintenance now
run_valve_maintenance.description: Run the valve maintenance cycle immediately for this Better Thermostat entity.

reset_heating_power.name: Reset heating power
reset_heating_power.description: Reset the heating power to its default value.

reset_pid_learnings.name: Reset PID learnings
reset_pid_learnings.description: Clear all learned PID state for this entity.

apply_pid_defaults.name: Apply PID defaults after reset
apply_pid_defaults.description: If enabled, seeds the current target bucket(s) with PID default gains (kp/ki/kd). You can override defaults below.

defaults_kp.name: Default kp
defaults_kp.description: Proportional gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.kp if not provided).

defaults_ki.name: Default ki
defaults_ki.description: Integral gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.ki if not provided).

defaults_kd.name: Default kd
defaults_kd.description: Derivative gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.kd if not provided).

test_boost.name: Test boost
test_boost.description: Manually trigger a Boost cycle on the configured Cooler entity, for testing wiring (target device, fan mode, threshold reachability) without needing to open and close a window.

state.window_open: turned off because a window was opened
state.window_close: resumed heating because a window was closed
state.summer_mode_on: turned off because the outdoor temperature is too high
state.summer_mode_off: resumed heating because the outdoor temperature dropped
state.degraded_mode_entered: entered degraded mode because some sensors are unavailable
state.degraded_mode_resolved: exited degraded mode because all sensors are available
state.door_open: turned off because a door was opened
state.door_close: resumed heating because a door was closed
